source.publisher: Larne Times (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: returned unopposed: four were nominated (Margt. E. M'Caughen, F. V. Simpson, John Hunter, Wm. M'Allister; Larne Times, 8 May 1952, p. 5) but the ward was not polled: Margaret V. M'Caughen thanks the electors 'for my unopposed return' (Larne Times, 22 May 1952, p. 5), North Ward was the only contest, and after the poll 'Councillor F. V. Simpson' is one of 'the only two Labour members of the Council' (Larne Times, 29 May 1952, p. 6)

note: Municipal elections, 21 May 1952: two councillors for each of the six wards; there was no election for aldermen, who held office until 1955. Sixteen nominations were received for the twelve seats; North Ward was the only contest after withdrawals in West Ward (Larne Times, 8, 22 and 29 May 1952). No party labels are printed for the unopposed members. The nomination list prints 'Margt. E. M'Caughen'; her own notice is signed Margaret V. M'Caughen. The two other nominees withdrew; F. V. Simpson, a retiring member seeking re-election, is placed on the new council by the report of the result. Returned unopposed.
